title: Migration EIP-712 domain separator hardcodes L1 chainId and lacks any per-message nonce or destination-L2 binding, enabling cross-deployment/multi-L2 signature reuse
description: The migration permit is signed on L1 and verified on L2. _domainSeparatorV4() builds the domain with C.getLegacyChainId() (a hardcoded constant = 1, Ethereum mainnet) and address(this). The struct hash covers only (owner, reciever, deadline) — there is no nonce and no field identifying the specific destination L2 / L2 Beanstalk deployment. Consequently a single owner signature is valid on any L2 deployment whose migration facet shares the same address(this) and the same hardcoded legacy chainId domain, and it carries no monotonically increasing nonce to bound reuse. This is the cross-chain authorization-scoping weakness underlying CC-001/CC-003: the permit is not scoped to a single chain/deployment nor to a single use. If Beanstalk migrates to (or redeploys on) more than one L2, or the diamond address is deterministic across L2s, the same signature is replayable across each.
impact: Cross-deployment / multi-L2 replay of a single migration signature and absence of a nonce that would otherwise bound CC-001. On a single-L2 deployment the practical impact is subsumed by CC-001; the standalone severity (signature not scoped to destination chain + no nonce) is Medium. The hardcoded legacy chainId also means the domain does not reflect the actual L2, so any future chainId-based replay protection is absent.

ite.intent: Scope each migration permit to exactly one chain, one deployment, and one use
ite.technique: Domain uses a hardcoded legacy chainId and address(this); struct hash omits nonce and destination-L2 identifier
ite.evasion: Reuse the same signature across deployments / repeatedly because nothing in the signed payload binds chain or usage count

ice_chain.corrupted_state: authorization scope: a single signature is valid across deployments and reusable
ice_chain.impact: Cross-L2 / repeated acceptance of one signature -> amplifies CC-001 replay and CC-003 redirection
ice_chain.exploit_path: obtain one L1 signature -> present it on any matching deployment / repeatedly -> verifySignature passes each time (no nonce, no destination binding)
